authority: Goals confirmed by the user in this project discussion; see the delivery registry separately for implementation and acceptance

items.title: New AI creators
items.statement: The first stage primarily serves new creators who use AI to make games. Opportunities for experienced mobile-game developers entering AI creation are also tested, without excluding people with no development experience.

items.title: Complex 2D and lightweight 3D
items.statement: The initial phase covers both 2D games with complex UI and lightweight 3D games; specific scale, quality, and device budgets remain to be defined.

items.title: Rendering and runtime core
items.statement: The rendering engine and runtime are the project's central components, seeking an approach suitable for the present and continuous iteration over the next two to three years.

items.title: Mixed presentation capabilities
items.statement: Support 3D scenes, characters, and effects while efficiently delivering complex 2D UI, skeletal animation, and frame-sequence animation.

items.title: Efficiency differentiation
items.statement: Carry forward historical strengths in compact high-performance execution, loading, base runtime packages, complex UI, power, and heat to establish contemporary advantages; specific leads and thresholds require verification with shared samples.

items.title: AI-native toolchain
items.statement: Combine Agent, Skills, MCP, and related ecosystems to help developers reduce cost, improve efficiency, and release creativity; specific interfaces, editors, and model choices await verification.

items.title: Creation and platform delivery
items.statement: Continue the integrated value of coding, UI, scenes, resources, animation, and platform publication for browsers, WeChat, Douyin, Meta Instant Games, Discord, Telegram, and native environments; initial order and support matrices are undetermined.

items.title: One-click AI migration of legacy projects
items.statement: Ultimately enable one-click import of original Egret projects and automatic conversion to the new engine through AI Agents, minimizing manual edits and intervention and achieving perfect execution after migration; complete migration and comparison acceptance are formal deliverables.

items.title: Continuing knowledge base and community
items.statement: Establish a sustainably maintained structured knowledge base, continuously iterating design principles, technical architecture, product composition, core advantages, and delivery goals, and supporting more open-source community participants.

items.title: Iteration research and independent positioning
items.statement: Study the last two years of iteration in Cocos, Laya, and Godot and changes in the industry ecosystem; learn problem-solving approaches to establish Egret's independent positioning and differentiated strengths.

items.title: Progressive design, research verification, and self-audit
items.statement: Gradually refine, research, deliberate, and technically verify the technical white paper, product requirements document, and engineering plan; maintain clear logic, avoid hallucinations, conduct self-audit and verification, and continuously iterate evidence and design.

items.title: Mature open-source implementations first, with layered verification
items.statement: When current environments cannot provide actual verification or exploration from scratch is too costly, first investigate mature GitHub implementations and repair records; expand rendering/runtime references to Three.js, Babylon.js, PlayCanvas, and others. Adopt established algorithms and mechanisms, focusing experiments on Egret adapters, differentiation, and real-device benefits to avoid redundant work. Execution is constrained by R015: research mature principles first, declare public libraries as explicit dependencies, and implement Egret core independently.

items.title: Fast compilation, debugging, and continuous iteration
items.statement: Optimize compilation, preview, and debugging waits for complex projects; study stable new TypeScript releases and replaceable build pipelines for rapid feedback during continuous human/AI edits. The historical time of under 30 seconds is not directly an accepted threshold for new projects.

items.title: Native SDK and cross-platform extension research
items.statement: Continue native App and embedded SDK Runtime paths; research Rust/C++, script VMs, and third-party library updates. Preserve extension room for future PC/Steam, D3D11/12, Vulkan, Metal, and GPU AI. Specific languages/libraries, initial desktop scope, and performance benefits still require tradeoff verification.

items.title: Independent core implementation and open-source community trust
items.statement: Design and implement Egret core independently from its own requirements and specifications; standards and open projects supply research foundations, while public infrastructure enters as explicit dependencies with versions, sources, notices, and modification records retained.

items.title: Complete modern engineering architecture and Egret-style code standards
items.statement: Redefine complete engineering architecture and code standards; retain Egret-style naming habits while allowing more rational modern project structure and APIs, giving developers familiarity without an old-style project form.

items.title: Start independent core implementation and investigate evidence gaps
items.statement: Attempt to start writing the core framework and logic, identifying missing supporting evidence and subjects requiring research.

items.title: Public collaboration and professional communication from early development
items.statement: Use public collaboration for code, design processes, documentation, and the knowledge base from early development. Communicate professionally and objectively; protect communication and materials unsuitable for publication; retain research references and acknowledgements; demonstrate Egret's independent design and innovation.

items.title: Chinese/English public materials and pre-push checks
items.statement: Before every GitHub push, complete English comments for critical code, organize all publishable documents and knowledge-base content, and provide complete Chinese and English reading documents and shared registered-status views. After completing the initial core source, documentation, and knowledge base, submit to the designated public repository.

items.title: Complete Spine animation support
items.statement: The engine must fully support Spine animation, preserving official semantics and authored effects within a publicly verified version/feature/backend/host matrix. Cover import, editing, complex UI and scene composition, events, resource recovery and applicable legacy migration without silently dropping features.
